evals.name: evaluation-trial-cancel-flow
evals.prompt: I'm reviewing the cancel-subscription flow for our meal-kit app, MossBowl. Right now: the cancel link is on a Settings sub-page called 'Plan health'. When you click it, you get a full-screen takeover with a photo of a half-empty fridge and the copy 'Are you sure? You'll lose your 7-day cooking streak.' Tapping 'Yes, cancel' opens a second screen offering 30% off for 3 months — and the only way to actually cancel is to scroll past three plan-comparison cards and tap a small grey 'No thanks, cancel anyway' link at the bottom. Our growth PM thinks this is fine because 'every SaaS does it.' I want a structured ethical critique I can take to the team — what's wrong, what to change, and what's actually OK to keep. Treat this seriously, I have a design review on Thursday.
evals.expected_output: Anti-Heroes evaluation that names specific cards (Trap-Setter, Empathy Manipulator, at minimum) tied to specific UI moments, pairs each with a Hero counter-move, distinguishes manipulative friction from necessary friction, and ends with shippable changes.

evals.name: reverse-brainstorm-finance-notifications
evals.prompt: We're scoping a new push-notification system for a personal finance app aimed at gen-z users (think: round-ups, savings nudges, 'you spent $14 on coffee this week'). Before we design the real version, my lead wants us to do a reverse brainstorm — design the worst possible notification system on purpose, the one that would make us hate ourselves, so we can make sure we're not slowly drifting into it. Then flip each anti-goal back into something we'd actually be proud of shipping. Help us run that exercise.
evals.expected_output: Reverse brainstorm output with explicitly named anti-goals tied to Anti-Hero cards (e.g., Empathy Manipulator, Nickeling-and-Diming, Puppeteer), worst-version notification examples, and Hero flips with concrete guardrails.

evals.name: ethical-dialogue-default-data-sharing
evals.prompt: ok so my team is tearing each other apart over whether to add a default-on toggle that shares aggregated user activity data with our 'partner ecosystem' (it's mostly so the BD team can show traction to potential integration partners). Half the team thinks it's fine because 'it's aggregated and there's a toggle in settings,' the other half thinks we're about to do something we'll regret. I have a 30-min meeting tomorrow morning to land this. Can you give me language and a short script I can use to facilitate this conversation without it turning into a fight? I want the ethical concern named clearly but not in a way that makes the BD lead feel attacked.
evals.expected_output: Ethical dialogue output with candidate Anti-Hero cards (Two-Faced, Puppeteer, Camouflager) named as language for the team, paired Hero counter-moves, a short non-accusatory script the user can actually say in the meeting, and follow-up questions that keep the conversation generative.
